subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw own and version a runtime-agnostic agent compatibility protocol for independently implemented non-Node runtimes?
rationale: The repository now owns reusable agent-core code, but deciding whether its concepts become a stable external protocol affects long-term API, security, compatibility, and product scope beyond a bounded implementation change.

options.title: Sponsor a portable-core RFC
options.body: Define the minimal protocol, capability model, versioning policy, conformance suite, and one constrained reference implementation before accepting runtime code.

options.title: Limit work to plugin JSON-RPC
options.body: Advance https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98004 for non-TypeScript plugins while leaving bare-metal agent implementations independent from OpenClaw compatibility guarantees.

options.title: Keep Node as the contract
options.body: Document MimiClaw and similar projects as independent inspirations without creating an OpenClaw-owned cross-runtime specification.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a portable-core RFC
recommendation.body: Define the minimal protocol, capability model, versioning policy, conformance suite, and one constrained reference implementation before accepting runtime code.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the strongest merged runtime-history signal and already handled the issue's product-direction discussion.
